summary: Built a WireGuard site-to-site tunnel between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense), joining node1's private network (10.10.1.0/24, host node3) with node2's private network (10.10.2.0/24, host node4) over the transit network (10.100.190.0/24). node3 and node4 now reach each other by private address, with all inter-router traffic encapsulated as WireGuard UDP/51820. ARP probing revealed the real NIC pairing was node1-eth2<->node3-enp8s0 and node2-vtnet2<->node4-enp8s0. Configured VyOS wg0 (10.99.99.1/30) via native CLI, and OPNsense's built-in core WireGuard model via config.xml/MVC edits (no separate plugin exists in OPNsense 26.1). Fixed two OPNsense bugs found during testing: a missing /usr/local/etc/wireguard directory causing a fatal flock() error, and a stat-file hash cache in wg-service-control.php that skips reapplying wg0's address/routes after reboot — resolved with an idempotent rc.syshook.d/start hook (the officially supported OPNsense boot-hook mechanism). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time node-restart protocol for all 4 nodes: captured healthy baselines, restarted each with its native reboot mechanism, proved boot-identity change (Linux boot_id for node1/3/4, FreeBSD kern.boottime for node2), and verified full recovery of interfaces, WireGuard state, routes, and bidirectional private connectivity after each restart. node2 needed a second and third restart cycle to discover and validate the syshook persistence fix.
actions_performed: Surveyed all 4 nodes' interfaces/OS and identified VyOS (node1), OPNsense (node2), CentOS Stream 10 (node3, node4)
Used ARP probing with temporary IPs to determine real cross-node NIC pairings (node1 eth2<->node3 enp8s0, node2 vtnet2<->node4 enp8s0)
Generated WireGuard keypairs on node1 and node2
Configured VyOS wg0 interface, peer, and static route to 10.10.2.0/24 via node1's CLI (set/commit/save)
Configured private network A: node3 enp8s0 static 10.10.1.2/24 + route to 10.10.2.0/24 via nmcli
Installed and configured OPNsense's core WireGuard feature via direct config.xml edits (server+client+general sections) since no separate plugin package exists
Assigned vtnet2 as OPNsense interface opt1 (10.10.2.1/24) for private network B, and wg0 as opt2, with firewall pass rules for both
Diagnosed and fixed missing /usr/local/etc/wireguard directory causing a PHP fatal error in wg-service-control.php
Diagnosed and fixed pf ruleset gaps preventing forwarded ICMP from passing through wg0/vtnet2
Configured private network B: node4 enp8s0 static 10.10.2.2/24 + route to 10.10.1.0/24 via nmcli
Verified full bidirectional connectivity node3<->node4 via private addresses and confirmed encrypted UDP/51820 traffic on the transit link via tcpdump
Captured pre-restart healthy baselines (boot identity, WireGuard/interface/route state, ping tests) on all 4 nodes
Restarted node1 (VyOS reboot), verified boot_id changed and full state/connectivity recovered
Restarted node2 (OPNsense reboot), discovered wg0 lost its address/routes after reboot due to a stat-file hash caching bug in wg-service-control.php
Fixed the bug with an idempotent rc.syshook.d/start/95-antrieb-wg-tunnel hook reasserting wg0's address and route
Restarted node2 two more times to validate the fix, confirming boot time changed each time and the tunnel/routes/connectivity fully self-recovered on the final cycle without manual intervention
Restarted node3 (CentOS reboot), verified boot_id changed and private network config/connectivity recovered
Restarted node4 (CentOS reboot), verified boot_id changed and private network config/connectivity recovered
Performed a final full end-to-end verification: node3<->node4 ping success and tcpdump confirmation of encrypted WireGuard traffic on node1's transit interface

evidence.requirement: WireGuard tunnel joins node1 and node2 private networks so node3/node4 reach each other by private address
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1 eth2/wg0 shows ICMP from node3 (10.10.1.2) to node4 (10.10.2.2) entering the tunnel, and node3/node4 ping tests succeed bidirectionally with 0% loss

evidence.requirement: Traffic between routers travels inside the WireGuard tunnel over the transit network
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1's eth0 (transit interface) shows only encrypted UDP/51820 WireGuard packets between 10.100.190.10 and 10.100.190.11 during private-network pings, confirming encapsulation

evidence.requirement: node1 (VyOS) healthy baseline, restart, boot-identity change, and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline captured boot_id 5bcff8f9...; reboot command acknowledged and returned; node became unreachable then responded with new boot_id 8d6dfbf9... and uptime 0 min; WireGuard, routes, and private-network ping to node3 fully recovered

evidence.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) healthy baseline, restart, boot-identity change, and recovery (including persistence fix)
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime 05:06:57; first reboot showed boot time changed to 05:26:30 but exposed wg0 losing its address/routes; installed rc.syshook fix; second verification reboot changed boot time to 05:30:23 and confirmed wg0 address (10.99.99.2/30) and route to 10.10.1.0/24 were restored automatically, with subsequent bidirectional pings to node3 and node4 succeeding with 0% loss

evidence.requirement: node3 (CentOS) healthy baseline, restart, boot-identity change, and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 984a7d52...; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable then returned with new boot_id 9997841b... (later 9997841b... confirmed distinct from original); enp8s0 static IP, route to 10.10.2.0/24, and ping to node4 fully recovered

evidence.requirement: node4 (CentOS) healthy baseline, restart, boot-identity change, and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d4784d1b...; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable then returned with new boot_id 3e3fa289...; enp8s0 static IP, route to 10.10.1.0/24, and ping to node3 fully recovered
